findings.message: Backtracking is required for the best endings. 'pick-the-lock' (threshold) needs both lock-pick (only from shop-pick) and flood-stamp (only from alley-clue). No single forward path visits both shop-pick and alley-clue. The only way is start > shop > shop-pick > gathering > 'gather-alley' > alley > alley-clue > gathering > drone-street (or the mirror order). That forces the reader to reread 'gathering' (draft lines 181-207, choices 'Ride back to Tam's shop' / 'Ride back to the dark alley') and, via the alley, pass a stop they may have seen. Endings 1 and 2 are only reachable this way. This is a route that goes back over pages already read to collect an item.

Continuity on short routes. ending-5 (line 433) says 'She walked back to Tam's shop. He gave her hot soup', and Tam says 'listen to the little voice'. A reader who went start > alley > gathering > lane never met Tam or had soup. The reader who skipped the alley never heard of Aunt Ila, yet ending-4 (line 413) says 'It was Aunt Ila' and 'the flood gate' with no setup. ending-3 (line 394) mentions Tam's shop shut, which is also unexplained on the alley route.

Validation brief check warns that 1 sentence exceeds the brief's 16-word limit (validation.r7.json brief.warnings). Likely the long sentences in dash-past line 253 ('A drone swung round, and its flash lit the whole street...') or ending-1 line 356. Literacy reviewer should confirm.

lockedHint on 'pick-the-lock' (line 286) tells the reader what is needed but not where to find it. With the backtracking problem above, a reader who locked out has no pointer to the shop or alley. Consider hinting at the places. Fair, but weak.
